item.title: Province seeking public feedback for upcoming 2027-2028 operating budget
item.description:
Province seeking public feedback for upcoming 2027-2028 operating budget jenniferdhogan Mon, 11/09/2026 - 15:20

Island residents are invited to share their priorities for the upcoming 2027-2028 operating budget.

Every year, the province invites residents, businesses, community organizations, and other stakeholder partners to share their input on what public programs and services should be prioritized in the operating budget. Everyone can engage in the budget consultation process by completing the online survey or sending an email submission (budgetsubmissions@gov.pe.ca) until January 10, 2027.

New this year, in-person information and engagement sessions are resuming to give all residents the opportunity to learn more about the budget process, the current economic situation for Prince Edward Island, and provide direct feedback to the Minister and the Department of Finance and Affordability. Registration is not required.

The four sessions will take place across the Island on the following dates and locations:

  • November 16, 6:00-8:00pm - Jack Blanchard Hall, 7 Pond St, Charlottetown, PE
  • November 23, 6:00-8:00pm - Mill River Resort, 180 Mill River Resort Rd. Route 136 Woodstock, PE. Simultaneous French interpretation will be available at this session only.
  • November 30, 5:00-7:00pm – Linkletter Community Centre, 1670 Route 11, Linkletter Rd, Linkletter, PE
  • December 7, 6:00-8:00pm – King’s Playhouse, 65 Grafton St, Georgetown, PE

Organizations and stakeholder partners are invited to participate in virtual consultations and must register by email (budgetsubmissions@gov.pe.ca) by November 18, 2026 to reserve their five-minute timeslot to present their priorities to the Minister of Finance and Affordability.

Learn more about pre-consultation consultations here.

item.title: Health PEI Launches new Applicant Tracking System
item.description:
Health PEI Launches new Applicant Tracking System jpranahan Fri, 11/06/2026 - 11:52

Health PEI has recently launched a new applicant tracking system (ATS), providing a more streamlined and user-friendly experience for individuals interested in health care careers across Prince Edward Island.

The new system makes it easier for candidates to search, filter, and apply for opportunities with Health PEI. The platform features a simplified application process, mobile-friendly design, and bilingual access in both English and French.

Applicants can create and manage a personal profile, apply to multiple job opportunities, track the status of their applications, and sign up for job alerts based on their areas of interest.

"Attracting and recruiting talented health care professionals is essential to strengthening our health system and improving access to care for Islanders. This new applicant tracking system modernizes the recruitment experience, making it easier for people to explore career opportunities, connect with Health PEI, and contribute to the delivery of health care across the province."

-  Minister of Health and Wellness, Cory Deagle

In addition to improving the candidate and employee experience, the platform also strengthens workforce planning by capturing key recruitment data, including application volumes, internal workforce trends, candidate qualifications, and time-to-hire metrics. 

"The applicant tracking system represents an important step forward in our efforts to attract and hire the health care professionals our province needs," said Pico Sine, Director of Workforce Recruitment with Health PEI. "By providing a simple and more accessible application experience, we’re making it easier for candidates to connect with job opportunities and for employees to grow their careers across our health care system.”

The launch of the new system is part of Health PEI's efforts to modernize recruitment processes and improve access for job seekers interested in building a health care career on Prince Edward Island.

Individuals interested in exploring career opportunities with Health PEI can visit Health PEI Jobs | JobsPEI to create a profile, sign up for job alerts, and apply for current opportunities.

item.title: Premier Lantz recognizes National Indigenous Veterans Day
item.description:
Premier Lantz recognizes National Indigenous Veterans Day jpranahan Fri, 11/06/2026 - 11:17

Premier Rob Lantz issued the following statement recognizing National Indigenous Veterans Day on November 8:

“Today, we honour the First Nations, Inuit and Métis men and women who have served Canada with courage and dedication.

For generations, Indigenous people have answered the call to serve—from the world wars to peacekeeping missions and military operations around the world.

Yet despite their service and sacrifice, many Indigenous veterans returned home to discrimination and were denied benefits and opportunities afforded to other veterans. This injustice is an important part of our country’s history, and it must not be overlooked.

Here on Prince Edward Island, we honour the service of Mi’kmaw veterans and recognize the lasting impact of their sacrifices on their families and communities.

National Indigenous Veterans Day is a time to remember those who lost their lives, honour those who returned home and recognize the generations of Indigenous families who have supported those who serve.

We owe it to these veterans and to future generations to preserve their stories, and ensure their contributions are never forgotten.

Lest we forget.”

item.title: Rural transit marks five years of serving Islanders
item.description:
Rural transit marks five years of serving Islanders jpranahan Thu, 11/05/2026 - 14:26

For the past five years, rural transit has helped Islanders get where they need to go by providing an affordable and reliable transportation option.

During that time, it has become an established part of the province’s transportation network by connecting rural communities with larger centres and making it easier for Islanders to access work, services and everyday needs.

“Over the past five years, rural transit has made a real difference for people in communities across PEI,” said Transportation and Infrastructure Minister Bloyce Thompson. “This milestone reflects the tremendous growth of the service, and we look forward to continuing to enhance it for Islanders in the years ahead.”

The provincial government recently signed a five-year agreement with Trius Transit to continue the rural transit service, giving it further stability and a stronger foundation for continued improvements. This supports the province’s commitment to safe, affordable, and sustainable transportation for Islanders.

“Affordability for people has been a cornerstone of rural transit,” Minister Thompson added. “Offering $2 one-way fare, low cost monthly passes and free travel for children and students from kindergarten to Grade 12, makes this a very valuable service for many Islanders.”

The next phase will focus on providing reliable, accessible service, with enough capacity to meet demand and improvements based on ridership trends and community feedback. 

“Rural transit can make a real difference in people’s lives,” said Trius Transit president Matthew Cassidy. “As we mark five years of this service on PEI, we’re proud to make transportation more accessible, convenient and affordable for Islanders.”

To accommodate growing ridership, larger motorcoach buses have been added to the Western PEI, Three Rivers and Montague routes, offering more seating and improved comfort for passengers.

Quick facts:

  • More than 550,000 one-way passenger trips have been taken since 2021. 
  • Rural transit has grown from three to eight year-round routes and services from Tignish to Souris. 
  • Monthly ridership has grown from about 1,500 trips in 2021 to almost 13,000 trips in 2026. 
  • Rural transit recorded 15,376 one-way trips in September 2026, the third-highest monthly total on record. 
  • Ridership reached 115,948 trips between January and September 2026, five per cent higher than during the same period in 2025. 
  • The North Shore summer shuttle provided more than 11,000 one-way trips in 2026.

For more information on schedules or to book a seat, visit the Trius Transit website.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
